day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect via metro or bus to your hotel, Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Keep it light tonight – rest is the priority.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a convenience store near Termini station or a 24-hour bar. Look for a tramezzino (Italian sandwich) or a slice of pizza al taglio for €2–4.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass (€28–€38) at the airport or Termini station to save on transport and museum entry. Validate your transport ticket every time you board. Keep your luggage secure at Termini – it's a busy hub late at night.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a leisurely breakfast, then head to the Vatican area. Visit St. Peter's Basilica (FREE entry) and climb to the top of St. Peter's Dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 on foot, €10 by elevator). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the basilica's stunning art and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across to the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (pre-booked online ticket ~€20, skip the line). Spend 3–4 hours immersed in one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book in advance online to avoid long queues and get the best price.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the Tiber River to the charming Trastevere neighborhood. Wander the cobblestone streets, admire street art, and soak in the lively evening atmosphere. Visit the beautiful Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free entry) before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a classic Italian breakfast at a local bar near the hotel – espresso + cornetto (croissant) for €2–3. Stand at the bar like a local to get the cheaper price.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick budget lunch near the Vatican at Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria) – famous pizza al taglio by weight, roughly €5–8 for a satisfying portion.
meals.dinner: Dine in Trastevere at Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello – classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or amatriciana for €10–14 per plate. Share dishes to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except last Sunday of the month, which is free but extremely crowded). Tuesday is a great day to visit. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) to enter St. Peter's Basilica – it's strictly enforced.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Borghese Gallery Art Experience (pre-booking MANDATORY, ~€15 + €2 booking fee). Discover Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate baroque villa. Entry is timed (2-hour slots), so book the first morning slot (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Arrive at least 15 minutes early.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, take a relaxing walk through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens (FREE) – Rome's version of Central Park. Then head to the nearby Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna) and toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain (free to view). Browse the upscale Via Condotti area window-shopping, then walk to the Pantheon (entry ~€5) – an architectural marvel nearly 2,000 years old.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Piazza Navona (free), a stunning baroque square with street performers and artists. Enjoy the golden hour light on the fountains before heading to dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh cornetto and cappuccino from a local bar near your hotel for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Try a budget-friendly lunch at Mercato di Campo de' Fiori – grab fresh produce, sandwiches, or street food for €4–7. The market is at its best in the morning but vendors remain until early afternoon.
meals.dinner: Near Piazza Navona, try Osteria dell'Anima or look for a set-price tourist menu (menù fisso) at €12–15 for starter, main, and water/wine. Avoid restaurants directly on the piazza – they charge tourist premiums.

day_by_day.notes: The Borghese Gallery only admits 360 visitors at a time and books out weeks in advance – book online as soon as possible at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery does not allow bags inside; there's a free cloakroom. Wear comfortable shoes – today involves a lot of walking.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring Ancient Rome. Visit the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill (combined ticket ~€16–18, book online). Arrive early (opening time ~9:00 AM) to avoid the worst heat and crowds. Allow 3–4 hours to fully explore the ancient ruins and imagine gladiatorial combat in the world's most famous amphitheater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Circus Maximus (free, outdoor site) and then up to the Aventine Hill to visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole – a quirky free attraction where you can spy a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome through a keyhole. Nearby, the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) offers a stunning panoramic view over Rome – completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood – Rome's foodie district and a great budget-friendly area. Browse the Testaccio Market (closes by afternoon, but the neighborhood is lively all evening) and explore the streets. This is a very local, non-touristy area of Rome.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel if included, or stop at a local bar for the usual espresso and cornetto (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local alimentari (deli) or supermarket near the Colosseum – grab bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit for €5–7. Eat in the shade near the Roman Forum.
meals.dinner: Dine in Testaccio at Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo (famous for thin-crust Roman pizza). Expect to spend €10–15 per person for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: June in Rome can be very hot (30°C+). Carry a reusable water bottle – Rome has hundreds of free public drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city with fresh, clean drinking water. Apply sunscreen and wear a hat when visiting the open-air ancient sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) – the world's oldest public museums, sitting atop Capitoline Hill with incredible views of the Roman Forum. See the original Marcus Aurelius bronze statue, Caravaggio paintings, and ancient Roman sculpture. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo (€15, or free with Roma Pass) – the massive cylindrical fortress with a rooftop terrace offering great views. Then walk along the scenic Via della Conciliazione back toward the Vatican area. Pop into any of the small free churches along the way – Rome's churches are filled with priceless art (Caravaggio, Raphael, Bernini) and are almost always free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed Friday evening in the Prati neighborhood (near the Vatican) – a popular local district with great restaurants, gelato shops, and bars. Join the Roman tradition of the passeggiata – an evening stroll before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Try a local bar in the Prati area for breakfast – ask for a 'caffè macchiato' and a 'cornetto integrale' (wholegrain croissant) for variety. €2–3.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local trattoria near Capitoline Hill – look for a 'pranzo' (lunch) special, often cheaper than dinner menus. Try supplì (fried rice balls, €1.50 each) as a Roman street food snack.
meals.dinner: In Prati, try Osteria dell'Angelo for authentic Roman cuisine at budget prices, or grab a budget-friendly dinner at one of the many trattorias on Via Cola di Rienzo. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Many of Rome's churches contain masterpieces that rival major museums – and they're free. Don't miss San Luigi dei Francesi (Caravaggio's St. Matthew cycle), Santa Maria del Popolo (two more Caravaggios), and San Pietro in Vincoli (Michelangelo's Moses). These are unmissable for art lovers on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj (€16) – a hidden gem of a private palazzo with an extraordinary art collection including works by Velázquez, Titian, Raphael, and Caravaggio. It's less crowded than major museums and offers an audio guide narrated by the current Prince Doria Pamphilj himself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring the Jewish Ghetto – one of Rome's oldest and most historically rich neighborhoods. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins (free, outdoor), browse local shops, and explore the area's unique character. Walk to the nearby Largo di Torre Argentina (free, outdoor archaeological site where Julius Caesar was assassinated). Then visit the Basilica di Santa Maria sopra Minerva – the only Gothic church in Rome, containing a Michelangelo sculpture (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Campo de' Fiori for the lively Saturday evening atmosphere. The square transforms into a social hub in the evenings. Enjoy a glass of local wine at a bar before dinner. Saturday night is perfect for a slightly more indulgent budget meal.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local forno (bakery) for fresh-baked goods – maritozzi (cream-filled buns, a Roman specialty) or pizza bianca. €2–4.
meals.lunch: Try Jewish-Roman cuisine in the Ghetto – look for carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes, €5–7) from a street vendor or small trattoria. This is a unique Roman culinary tradition.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly on Saturday – try a mid-range trattoria near Campo de' Fiori. Enjoy a full Roman meal: antipasto, pasta, secondi, and a carafe of house wine (vino della casa) for €18–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings are great for visiting local markets. The Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (Sunday mornings) is worth noting for tomorrow. If you want to visit any major museums, Saturday afternoons can get crowded – plan accordingly. Carry cash as many small restaurants and trattorias in Rome are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the Porta Portese Flea Market in Trastevere (open Sunday mornings from 6:00 AM to 2:00 PM) – Rome's largest and most famous flea market. Browse vintage items, antiques, clothing, and local curiosities. This is a great free cultural experience and a chance to pick up unique souvenirs at bargain prices. Practice your bargaining!
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon revisiting your favorite spots or checking off anything you missed. Consider a visit to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (€10) in the Villa Borghese area for modern Italian art. Alternatively, simply wander through the Trastevere and Gianicolo Hill area – the viewpoint at Gianicolo offers arguably the best panoramic view of Rome (free, accessible by bus 115 from Trastevere).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your final evening in Rome with a farewell dinner. Return to your favorite neighborhood from the week or try somewhere new. After dinner, take one last walk past the illuminated Trevi Fountain, Pantheon, and Piazza Navona – Rome at night is magical and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries and fruit from the Porta Portese market vendors for a fun on-the-go breakfast. €3–5.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a relaxed Sunday lunch – Romans take this seriously. Find a trattoria offering a Sunday lunch special (pranzo della domenica). Many offer set menus with multiple courses for €15–20.
meals.dinner: For your farewell dinner, splurge slightly on a memorable meal. Try cacio e pepe, carbonara, or saltimbocca alla Romana at a well-reviewed local trattoria. Budget €20–25 per person including wine – you've earned it!

day_by_day.notes: Note your departure details and arrange transport back to the airport in advance. The Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino Airport runs regularly (€14, ~32 min) and is the most reliable option. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey and airport check-in. The last Vatican Museums entry on the last Sunday of the month is FREE but extremely crowded – avoid if June 21 falls on the last Sunday of the month.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (30 min, ~€14), then taxi or rideshare to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and freshen up.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel — look for a 24-hour bar or pizzeria al taglio (pizza by the slice) for a light arrival snack around €8–12

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival, keep Day 1 simple. Confirm hotel has 24-hour reception. Lay out your Day 2 plan before sleeping so you can hit the ground running. Pack comfortable walking shoes for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Ease into Rome with a leisurely Italian breakfast at a local café near the hotel — espresso, cornetto, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Then take a relaxed orientation stroll through your neighborhood to get your bearings, stopping to admire any nearby piazzas or churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Borghese Gallery Art Experience (book timed entry in advance — entry is strictly ticketed in 2-hour slots). Discover Bernini's breathtaking sculptures including Apollo and Daphne and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate baroque villa. Afterward, walk through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down Via Veneto for the classic Roman evening atmosphere, then enjoy dinner in the Prati or Parioli neighborhood — elegant yet relaxed trattorias perfect for a mid-range budget.

meals.breakfast: Café bar near hotel — cornetto + cappuccino (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — grab supplies from a nearby alimentari (deli): fresh bread, prosciutto, local cheese, and fruit (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium area or Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — classic Roman pasta like cacio e pepe or amatriciana (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked in advance — only 360 visitors allowed per 2-hour session. Book at least 2–3 weeks ahead at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Explore the vast collection of papal art, the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate with Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Allow 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit through St. Peter's Square and visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) — climb the dome for panoramic views of Rome (~€8). Afterward, cross the Tiber and explore the charming Trastevere neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local wines, and traditional street food. A perfect immersive introduction to Roman cuisine culture.

meals.breakfast: Quick espresso and pastry before the Vatican — Bar San Pietro near Piazza Risorgimento (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Trastevere — try Tonnarello or a local pizzeria for a classic margherita or Roman-style thin-crust pizza (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tasting experience — supplement with a glass of house wine at a wine bar (~€5–8 extra)

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets online in advance to skip the notoriously long queues — same-day entry is nearly impossible in June. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica. The evening food walk typically lasts 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour — explore Rome's most authentic covered market where locals shop daily. Sample cured meats, aged cheeses, fresh produce, and street food. Then dive into the city's bold offal tradition with supplì, porchetta sandwiches, and more adventurous Roman delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, walk off breakfast with a visit to the nearby Pyramid of Cestius and the Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) — a serene, beautiful hidden gem in Testaccio (~€3 donation). Then head to Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with sweeping city panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with an Aperitivo hour — Rome's version of happy hour with free snacks included. Then enjoy a leisurely dinner in the Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's culinary heartland.

meals.breakfast: Included as part of the Testaccio Market food tour tastings
meals.lunch: Eat your way through the market — budget €15–20 for additional tastings, a sandwich, and fresh juice at the market stalls
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto or Remo in Testaccio — classic Roman trattoria with rigatoni alla carbonara, saltimbocca, and tiramisu (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is closed on Sundays. If Day 4 falls on a Sunday, swap this activity with the Ancient Rome tour from Day 5. The offal food tour is adventurous — if tripe or offal isn't appealing, let the guide know and they can suggest alternatives at the market.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Ancient Rome & Palatine Hill Guided Tour — walk through the Roman Forum, climb Palatine Hill for sweeping panoramic views over the ancient city, and explore the Colosseum with expert historical commentary. Allow 4–5 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, visit the Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums) on Capitoline Hill — home to the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning art collections (~€15). Enjoy rooftop terrace views over the Forum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the historic center for the classic Roman passeggiata (evening stroll). Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain, explore the Spanish Steps at golden hour, and browse the boutiques around Via Condotti.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bar near the Colosseum area (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick stop at a nearby alimentari before the tour, or grab a panino near the Colosseum (~€10–14) — avoid tourist trap restaurants in this zone
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso or Osteria della Trippa in the historic center — enjoy Roman classics like coda alla vaccinara or abbacchio (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum + Forum + Palatine Hill combo tickets online well in advance — June is peak season and timed entry sells out fast. The guided tour often includes skip-the-line access. Wear sunscreen and bring water as Palatine Hill has minimal shade in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to Rome's Baroque art scene — visit the Church of San Luigi dei Francesi to see Caravaggio's stunning St. Matthew cycle (free), then walk to Sant'Agostino for another Caravaggio. Continue to the Piazza Navona area to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Campo de' Fiori market (morning winding down by noon — browse remaining stalls) and the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and browse the unique shops and bakeries. Consider visiting the Palazzo Spada with its famous trompe-l'œil perspective gallery (~€5).
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a special dinner experience — this is your second-to-last evening in Rome. Enjoy a proper sit-down meal with Roman classics and local wine in a candlelit setting.

meals.breakfast: Caffè Sant'Eustachio near the Pantheon — one of Rome's most famous coffee bars, known for its exceptional espresso (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Jewish-Roman cuisine in the Ghetto — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and baccalà fritto at Nonna Betta or Ba'Ghetto (~€22–28)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio or Il Pagliaccio area — elevated mid-range Roman dining with seasonal tasting menus (~€40–55 per person with wine)

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges an entry fee (~€5). If time allows, it's worth a visit this morning before the Caravaggio churches. June evenings are long and warm — perfect for lingering over dinner outdoors on a terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore anything you missed. Consider a visit to the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) for a contemporary contrast to the week's classical art, or simply return to Villa Borghese gardens for a peaceful farewell stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — head to the artisan shops near Campo de' Fiori or Via del Governo Vecchio for unique, non-touristy gifts: handmade leather goods, local ceramics, specialty food items (truffle products, pasta, biscotti), and art prints.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner — return to your favorite restaurant from the week or try something new. Enjoy a long, leisurely Roman dinner with antipasto, pasta, secondi, dessert, and digestivo (limoncello or amaro). Savor every bite.

meals.breakfast: Slow, indulgent final Italian breakfast at a café with a view — cornetto, cappuccino, and fresh juice (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch — Roman-style suppli and pizza al taglio from a quality street food spot (~€10–15) to save room for a big farewell dinner
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite discovery of the trip or try Armando al Pantheon — a beloved Roman institution near the Pantheon with impeccable traditional Roman cuisine (~€35–45 per person). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure logistics: if flying out the next morning, arrange an early taxi or shuttle to Fiumicino the night before. Allow 2+ hours before flight time for check-in and security. Pack your bags the night before to enjoy a stress-free final morning in the Eternal City.

meals.dinner: Ristorante Paris in Trastevere – a Roman institution offering cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and a curated wine list in a romantic setting

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance booking – strictly limited to 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. Concierge should secure this weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for the Trastevere evening walk on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Private skip-the-line access to the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel with an expert art historian guide. Begin at 08:00 for the quietest experience, exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber to Castel Sant'Angelo for panoramic rooftop views of Rome. Explore the Prati neighborhood – Rome's elegant district near the Vatican – for boutique browsing and a leisurely coffee break at a sidewalk café.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive dinner reservation at Il Sorpasso or Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio – refined Roman cuisine in a sophisticated atmosphere. Optional: post-dinner gelato at Fatamorgana (gourmet artisanal flavors).

meals.breakfast: Early in-resort breakfast at 07:00 before Vatican departure – espresso, yogurt, pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati – beloved local spot serving traditional Roman dishes like rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio al forno (lamb)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio near the Pantheon – seasonal tasting menu with sommelier-paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Vatican visit should be booked as a private early-access tour (08:00 opening). The experience lasts approximately 3–3.5 hours. Dress code enforced at Vatican: covered shoulders and knees required.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – join a private culinary guide at Rome's most authentic covered market. Taste seasonal produce, aged cheeses, cured meats, and dive into Rome's cucina povera heritage with suppli, mortadella, and porchetta tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ancient Rome & Palatine Hill Guided Tour – a private archaeologist-led experience through the Roman Forum, Palatine Hill (birthplace of Rome), and the Colosseum exterior. Marvel at two millennia of history in a single afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on Aventine Hill with views of St. Peter's dome through the Knights of Malta keyhole – one of Rome's most magical hidden secrets. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast with a focus on local Roman pastries and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Testaccio Market tour serve as a generous late-morning meal; supplement with a light plate at Flavio al Velavevodetto – a beloved Testaccio trattoria carved into a hill of ancient pottery shards
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant at Palazzo Manfredi – Rome's most dramatic dining experience with a private terrace directly overlooking the Colosseum; Michelin-starred cuisine with a degustation menu

day_by_day.notes: Aroma Restaurant is one of Rome's most sought-after reservations – book at least 4–6 weeks in advance. The Colosseum view from the terrace at sunset is extraordinary. Testaccio tour is best enjoyed on an empty stomach.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a Roman chef at a luxury culinary studio. Learn to make fresh pasta (tonnarelli cacio e pepe), Roman-style artichokes (carciofi alla giudia), and tiramisu from scratch. Enjoy your creations as a mid-morning brunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic centro storico at leisure – Piazza Navona, the Pantheon (now requiring timed entry), and the elegant Via Condotti for luxury shopping (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi flagship stores). Visit Fendi's Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana for an art and fashion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private after-hours access experience at a Roman art venue (arrange through concierge) or an evening at the Teatro dell'Opera di Roma if a performance is scheduled. Nightcap at the rooftop bar of a five-star hotel overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: Light in-resort breakfast before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Feast on your own creations during the cooking class – this serves as a full lunch experience
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio – Rome's two-Michelin-star restaurant offering a bold contemporary Italian tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings; one of the finest dining experiences in the city

day_by_day.notes: Book Il Pagliaccio well in advance – it is one of only two two-Michelin-star restaurants in Rome. Smart dress required. The cooking class should be arranged through the resort concierge with a private instructor for a bespoke experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to the ancient Roman port city of Ostia Antica via private car – a less-visited but extraordinarily preserved archaeological site rivaling Pompeii. Explore mosaics, bathhouses, temples, and amphitheaters with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome and visit the Capitoline Museums – the world's oldest public museums, housing the iconic She-Wolf sculpture, Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, and sweeping Forum views from the terrace. Guided private tour recommended.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration dinner at a prestigious Roman restaurant. Enjoy a long, indulgent Italian meal with multiple courses, fine wine, and exceptional service – the Roman way.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet resort breakfast before the early departure to Ostia Antica
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch prepared by the resort or a nearby Ostia Antica café – enjoy al fresco among ancient ruins
meals.dinner: La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri – Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, helmed by Heinz Beck; a transcendent dining experience with panoramic city views, a 60,000-bottle wine cellar, and an unforgettable tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Rome dining – reserve 6–8 weeks in advance, smart formal dress required. Ostia Antica is approximately 30 minutes from central Rome by private car. Combine both experiences for a rich cultural and culinary day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – slow, luxurious breakfast at the resort. Take a private sunrise walk or photography tour of Rome's most iconic piazzas (Piazza del Popolo, Spanish Steps, Trevi Fountain) before the crowds arrive. Toss a coin at the Trevi Fountain to ensure your return.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping or souvenir curation – visit Eataly Roma for premium Italian pantry goods (aged balsamic, truffle products, artisan pasta) to bring home. Optional: a final espresso ritual at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè, widely regarded as Rome's finest coffee bar.
day_by_day.evening: Private chauffeur transfer to Fiumicino Airport. Enjoy the resort's farewell amenity (a bottle of wine or sweet treat for the journey). Depart Rome with extraordinary memories.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort – order everything you loved during the week; savor it slowly
meals.lunch: Casual but excellent lunch at Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina – a legendary Roman deli and restaurant beloved by locals and food lovers worldwide; try the carbonara and the cheese selection
meals.dinner: Airport dining or onboard – pack Eataly provisions for a gourmet in-flight snack

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Fiumicino Airport, especially on a Sunday. Request a late checkout from the resort to maximize your final Roman afternoon. Roscioli requires a reservation even for lunch on weekends.
